_doc: Agent Triforge — Antigravity permission guardrails, expressed in agy's action(target) syntax. Enforcement evidence lives in the newest ops/research/*-probe-record.md (rows AGY-08/09/10 and the native-mode rows AGY-12/13/16).

This file is documentation + a mergeable block. templates/.antigravity/settings.json ships the same `permissions` object for project bootstrap (it records deny INTENT — project-tier settings.json is not read headless, see below). The only settings tier agy documents and enforces headless is the user tier, ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json; a user who wants the denies enforced merges this block there by hand. Triforge never writes the user tier (R18).

Deny intent — three `command(<prefix>)` actions. agy's shell tool is `run_command` and its permission action is `command`; `run_shell_command` was the Gemini-CLI tool name and agy has no such tool (a `run_shell_command(...)` deny entry matches nothing):
git push -> deny: command(git push)  (subagents never touch remotes — the lead promotes)

Per-agent shell denial: the flat deny vocabulary has no per-agent scoping, so it is expressed in each agent's frontmatter instead. All four agents carry `commandExecutionPolicy: "off"` and omit `run_command` and `write_to_file` from `tools` (4.2): the omission IS the denial. They return their answer and the lead saves it. Tool names and permission actions differ on purpose: the tools are `view_file`, `write_to_file` and `run_command`, and agy's permission actions for them are `read_file`, `write_file` and `command`.

Enforcement facts (agy 1.2.x, re-probed 2026-09-11): AGY-08 — project-tier hooks written in the documented `.agents/hooks.json` named-hook shape (events PreInvocation/PostInvocation/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop) FIRED headless on agy 1.2.0 (lead marker-file re-probe, 05:03) — the July 'hooks inert headless' finding was a probe-shape error — the harness re-run on agy 1.2.1 the same evening recorded FAIL with both hooks.json files loaded, and the 2026-09 record (2026-09-27) recorded PASS on agy 1.2.12 with all five events fired; headless agy hooks remain an open watch, never an enforcement path, and Triforge ships none and relies on none. AGY-09 — deny rules do NOT survive --dangerously-skip-permissions, so the invocation helper never passes that flag. AGY-10 — --sandbox does not confine, so it is not used. Project-tier settings.json (.gemini/, .agents/, .antigravity/) is NOT read headless.

What enforces what: (1) the per-agent `tools` allowlist + `commandExecutionPolicy` in agents/*.md is the PRIMARY guardrail in native mode (TRIFORGE_AGY_MODE=native, or the default, auto, when `agy agents` lists the name; KTD10, D-042: AGY-12 and AGY-16). (2) Injection mode (TRIFORGE_AGY_MODE=injection, or auto when the name is not listed) runs agy's default agent, whose tools include a write tool and a shell. (3) In every mode invoke_antigravity passes session rules with --settings where `agy --help` names that flag (_agy_lane_settings; never saved, no tier written): deny write_file(*) and command(*), allow read_file(*), deny reads of the credential paths the other read-only lanes refuse, and the user's own user-tier rules carried along. Read live on agy 1.5.1, 2026-11-05: a permission prompt headless ends the turn at once with an empty response, while a deny rule hands the model a tool error and the turn goes on to its answer; a rule's target is an exact path, a directory prefix or `*` (AGY-19). An action no rule covers, such as read_url, still surfaces in `denied_actions` and, with an empty response, fails naming the user-tier allow rule. The lease lane's agy builder is a separate path and gets no session rules.
